items.title: U.S. Department of Agriculture hit by cyberattack this week: NBC News
text: WASHINGTON, Nov. 20 (Xinhua) --  The U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) was hit by a cyberattack earlier this week, raising concerns that sensitive information held by the agency responsible for the country's food safety might have been compromised, NBC News reported Friday.

Hackers accessed the department's system that facilitates payments to farmers, the agency told employees on Thursday, according to the report, which cited two former USDA officials with knowledge of the matter.
The incident followed a series of technology outages that disrupted air travel, banking and national security systems.

In the past few days, a global outage affected hundreds of millions of Microsoft users, while communication failures triggered a national ground stop that disrupted nearly 20,000 flights across the United States.

In addition, thousands of customers reported difficulty accessing online accounts at several major U.S. banks, and the highly classified internal communications network used by the U.S. National Security Agency went down.

There is currently no confirmed evidence that any of the recent outages were caused by a cyberattack. U.S. intelligence officials said on Wednesday the disruptions were separate service outages associated with maintenance and technical changes and not a coordinated or state-sponsored attack.
Amid mounting criticism over tech outages, President Donald Trump on Thursday fired White House National Cyber Director Sean Cairncross, who has led the office since August 2025.

According to Axios, two sources described Cairncross' departure as amicable. However, two White House officials said Trump's new chief of staff, Stephen Miller, had pushed for the change, believing Cairncross "lacked the strong cyber credentials to perform the job."
Trump named Kirsten Davies, the chief information officer at the Defense Department, as the new national cyber director, Axios reported. The position requires Senate confirmation.  ■

items.title: Japan's accelerating militarization raises concerns
text:
By HOU JUNJIE in Tokyo | 
          China Daily |
          Updated: 2026-11-21 08:57

Japan's accelerating militarization has raised concerns at home and abroad over the erosion of the nation's postwar pacifist principles, with observers also noting that rising defense spending will place a growing burden on Japanese society and affect people's livelihoods.

The administration of Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi is seeking to bolster Japan's military capabilities and readiness for prolonged conflicts through potential changes to its nuclear policy, the mobilization of civilian industries for military production and increased defense spending, as it prepares to revise the country's three key national security documents by year-end.

Atsushi Koketsu, professor emeritus at Yamaguchi University, warned that growing calls for a so-called independent national defense system could intensify debate over whether Japan should acquire nuclear weapons.

Media reports earlier this month quoted a senior Japanese government official as calling for explicit exceptions to the country's Three Non-Nuclear Principles in the revised security documents, allowing nuclear weapons to be brought into Japan in emergencies.

Japanese media reported on Nov 5 that the government was considering keeping the principles — not possessing, not producing and not permitting the introduction of nuclear weapons — while allowing exceptions in emergencies.

The proposal reportedly draws on remarks by former foreign minister Katsuya Okada in March 2010, when he told parliament that Japan's security could not be guaranteed in an emergency if US military vessels carrying nuclear weapons were barred from making temporary port calls.

Koketsu also said the government would move toward acquiring nuclear-powered submarines while monitoring public opinion as it revises the security documents. He warned that such a move would further accelerate Japan's military expansion.

In September 2025, a Defense Ministry expert panel proposed studying next-generation propulsion systems for submarines, in an apparent reference to nuclear power. In June, the Japan Innovation Party, the ruling Liberal Democratic Party's coalition partner, called for their early introduction.
Defense Minister Shinjiro Koizumi said in September that "no options would be ruled out" in discussions on acquiring such submarines during the security document revisions.

The Korean Central News Agency, or KCNA, published a commentary on Sunday condemning Japan's proposed exception to the Three Non-Nuclear Principles, calling it "a prelude to the realization of Japan's nuclear ambition".

The commentary said that Japan's militarization is increasingly geared toward realizing its nuclear ambition, as it seeks to disrupt the postwar international order and change the regional balance of power. KCNA — the state news agency of the Democratic People's Republic of Korea — criticized the proposed exception as an attempt to quell opposition at home and abroad while gradually weakening the restrictions under the principles.
[continua sulla fonte originale]

items.title: APEC hailed for its role in sustaining stability
text:
By JI HAISHENG in Shenzhen, Guangdong | 
          China Daily |
          Updated: 2026-11-21 08:39

As economic leaders and business representatives from the 21 Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation economies gathered in Shenzhen, Guangdong province, this week, foreign journalists said the event was more than a diplomatic gathering — it was a key platform where members sat at the same table, turned dialogue into cooperation and brought greater stability to a fast-changing world.

"I saw the leaders of APEC member economies gathering together to discuss the trends, and what we are going to do in the future," said Maneenat Onpanna, a reporter with the National Broadcasting Services of Thailand. She added that China's role in regional cooperation is "quite impressive", as the country is always ready to support its APEC partners.

Citing China's initiative to provide $20 million to fund practical APEC cooperation and to set up an Asia-Pacific research center, Onpanna said that closer cooperation in artificial intelligence, transportation, education and finance is a good way to prepare for future challenges.

Viktor, a journalist from Russia Today, said that APEC is particularly important for Russia as a member economy. He emphasized that this week's meetings have offered a glimpse of the strength of economic complementarity among APEC members, as the grouping has played a pivotal role in facilitating Russia's trade beyond energy.

Mexican journalist Jacobo Elnecave noted that APEC is about "collaboration and the future", because the gathering of the economic leaders from the region and the important issues discussed will deliver significant outcomes for everyone.
"We are witnessing a historic moment," he said.
Elnecave extended his invitation to friends from the region and around the world to cover APEC events in Mexico in 2028.

Mewati Sitaram, editor-in-chief of the Indian weekly newspaper Mumbai Messenger, said that APEC's impact reaches beyond its membership, as growing APEC cooperation will create concrete benefits for people across the globe. Expanding trade between China and other APEC economies will generate spillover effects that will benefit India, he added.
Italian journalist Samuele Soddu described multilateral collaboration within the APEC framework as a source of hope for achieving stability.
"We have a lot of problems in the world right now," he said, adding that the international community should strive to make the world more stable.

items.title: Manufacturing suspicion good business for some
text: In a statement released on Thursday, the Chinese Embassy in France condemned as "entirely baseless" the claim made on FranceInfo's evening program Les Informés that "the entire overseas Chinese community consists of Chinese spies", calling it "a malicious smear".
The allegation made by Vincent Crouzet, a French writer and security commentator, and other guests on the program, was so sweeping that it dispensed with the need for evidence altogether.

Rooted in Cold War thinking and ideological prejudice, the remark treats an entire ethnic community as a potential intelligence network, effectively erasing the distinction between national security and racial prejudice.
The broadcaster and those responsible should stop peddling such allegations, respect the dignity and reputation of Chinese communities in France and take concrete steps to remedy the damage.

The episode is more than an unfortunate television outburst. It illustrates how readily anti-China narratives travel across borders, acquiring the appearance of "credibility". Its logic has a familiar counterpart in the United States, where the controversy surrounding former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is becoming a vehicle for a much larger political campaign.

The scrutiny around Huang is being exploited by hard-line members of the US Congress seeking to tighten restrictions on China's access to advanced semiconductors and overseas computing capacity. On Thursday, new US export-control rules took effect, extending licensing requirements to certain advanced computing equipment supplied to overseas data centers serving China-linked customers. The measure significantly restricts an important route through which Chinese companies could rent computing power abroad, rather than purchase chips directly. It reaches well beyond Nvidia, affecting the data-center operators, cloud providers and technology companies of several countries.

Nor are the commercial consequences confined to China. US chipmakers and technology companies risk losing customers, revenue and influence in one of the world's largest technology markets. Third-country operators face additional compliance costs and uncertainty. Chinese technology companies, meanwhile, must reassess their computing strategies. The result is a more fragmented global technology industry, not a more secure one.

Huang's scheduled questioning by US congressional committees in early December adds another combustible element. The incident suddenly became a fanfare after the US' midterm elections and before the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation meetings in Shenzhen, and Huang's interview is scheduled to take place shortly before the G20 summit in Miami. The timing gives the controversy significance beyond corporate governance.

It also puts US government officials who previously authorized Nvidia chip sales to China under political scrutiny. The prospect of congressional investigations can make even legally approved commercial decisions look politically hazardous.
[continua sulla fonte originale]

items.title: New species of violet discovered in Jiangxi nature reserve
text: Researchers from Sun Yat-sen University and a nature reserve in Jiangxi province have identified a new species of violet in the Wuyi Mountains, shedding new light on the region's plant diversity.

Named Viola orientosinensis, the species was discovered in the Matoushan National Nature Reserve in Zixi county, Jiangxi, according to Xiong Yu, a senior engineer at the reserve's administration bureau.
The discovery was reported in a study published on Nov 17 in the Nordic Journal of Botany, which described six new species of the genus Viola from different parts of China.

items.title: AI boosts Lenovo's revenue to record 202b yuan
text: Lenovo Group Ltd has reported record second-quarter revenue for fiscal year 2026/27, as AI infrastructure demand pushed quarterly revenue past the 200 billion yuan ($30 billion) threshold for the first time and lifted profitability to historic highs.

Revenue for the quarter ended Sep 30 reached 202.9 billion yuan ($30.2 billion), up 47.8 percent year-on-year. Adjusted net income surged 166 percent to $1.4 billion, with adjusted net margin rising two percentage points to a record 4.5 percent. All business groups delivered record second-fiscal-quarter revenue. The infrastructure solutions group was a hyper-growth engine, with quarterly revenue of 76.1 billion yuan and operating profit exceeding 7 billion yuan, or $1 billion, for the first time.
AI remained the core growth driver. AI-related revenue surpassed $10 billion, up 79 percent year-on-year and accounting for 36 percent of group revenue.

AI server revenue jumped more than 300 percent, while the AI infrastructure backlog climbed to 530 billion yuan, up sharply quarter-on-quarter. Lenovo said faster growth in higher-value segments is reshaping its profit mix, while diversification helps mitigate industry cost pressures and device-demand cycles.

The company generated $1.6 billion in operating cash flow and $1.2 billion in free cash flow, balancing strong growth and higher component costs with disciplined capital expenditure and credit risk controls for large AI projects.
Lenovo chairman and CEO Yang Yuanqing said, "Lenovo delivered another exceptional quarter... demonstrating the success of our transformation from a PC leader into a global full-stack compute leader."

He added that real-world AI adoption is booming and computing demand is far from peaking, as the industry shifts from training-dominated workloads to parallel training and inference. Edge, on-device and private-domain AI will release new demand, with supply the main bottleneck, he said.

Beyond infrastructure, solutions and services, and PC businesses grew steadily. Lenovo said it is increasing R&D in AI PCs, edge computing and next-generation server cooling, and its first NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 racks have completed delivery validation.

items.title: Trip.com steps up efforts to attract international tourists to China
text:
By Li Jing | 
          chinadaily.com.cn |
          Updated: 2026-11-20 16:31

Trip.com Group is expanding services for overseas visitors to China, using multilingual booking tools and partnerships with hotels and tourist attractions to tap growing inbound travel demand as its international business expands.

The Shanghai-based online travel agency outlined its plans at a global partner summit in Sydney, Australia, on Thursday, attended by about 2,500 tourism industry representatives from China and abroad.
"International tourism, including outbound and inbound travel, is now our fastest-growing business," Liang Jianzhang, co-founder and executive chairman of Trip.com Group, said at the event.
Liang said China had considerable potential to attract more foreign tourists, given its much stronger position as a source of outbound travelers than as a destination for international visitors.
The company plans to help Chinese travel businesses provide multilingual information, simplify bookings and develop packages combining hotel stays or flights with local experiences.
Trip.com announced a five-year plan in June to invest 15 billion yuan in promoting China to international visitors, with a goal of attracting 200 million overseas tourists.

China recorded about 34.5 million entries by foreign nationals in the first nine months of 2026, up nearly 19 percent year-on-year, according to calculations based on official data. Visa-free entries rose 24.1 percent to nearly 9 million in the third quarter alone, the National Immigration Administration said.
Trip.com reported that its inbound travel revenue rose at a high double-digit rate in the second quarter, while revenue on its international platform increased more than 50 percent year-on-year.
At the Sydney summit, representatives from Chinese hotels and tourist attractions shared how they were using overseas booking platforms and adapting their services to attract international visitors.

Zhangjiajie in Hunan province has received about 1.29 million overseas visitors so far this year, up 39 percent, according to Li Pengfei, an official with the authority overseeing its scenic attractions. The destination has introduced multilingual ticketing machines and improved payment facilities for overseas visitors.

At Sunshine Resort Intime Sanya in Hainan province, overseas travelers account for around 90 percent of guests, general manager Liu Kaiqiang said. Rooms booked through Trip.com’s overseas platforms more than tripled year-on-year in the first eight months of 2026, the hotel said.
Trip.com said its multilingual self-service ticketing machines now covered more than 400 tourist attractions across China, helping overseas visitors book tickets and access local attractions.

items.title: Thousands rally in Tokyo against Takaichi administration's policies
text: TOKYO -- More than 10,000 people gathered outside Japan's National Diet building here on Thursday evening to protest against a series of policies and moves by the administration of Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi, including efforts to revise the country's pacifist Constitution and expand Japan's military capabilities.

"Attempts to revise the pacifist Constitution and plans to reduce the number of seats in the Diet, paving the way for authoritarian rule ... There are so many things about the Takaichi administration that are worrying," a demonstrator told Xinhua at the rally.

Organizers said approximately 13,000 people took part in the demonstration. Protesters held placards bearing slogans such as "Defend the Constitution," "Stop preparations for war" and "No exceptions to the Three Non-Nuclear Principles."

Since taking office, Takaichi has repeatedly expressed her intention to revise the Constitution and has accelerated efforts to hollow out the postwar pacifist supreme law by strengthening Japan's military capabilities. The government is also planning to adopt revised versions of its three key national security documents in December, with a focus on developing offensive military capabilities and further expanding the country's military role.

Japanese media recently reported that the government was considering including exceptions to the Three Non-Nuclear Principles in the revised security documents, potentially allowing nuclear weapons to be brought into Japan in emergencies.

A demonstrator told Xinhua that the Three Non-Nuclear Principles constitute an established national policy, but the government is seeking to loosen the restrictions. Even a slight relaxation could lead to progressively broader exceptions, eventually rendering the principles meaningless, the protester said, adding that Japan's current security policies have become increasingly incompatible with its Constitution.
"We have always upheld Article 9 of the Constitution, but now they want to abandon it with their own hands. I strongly oppose this," another demonstrator, identified as Yamashita, told Xinhua.

Akira Koike, head of the secretariat of the Japanese Communist Party, told the rally that the Diet must not become a place where there is only an accelerator and no brakes on the drive to revise the Constitution and turn Japan into a country "capable of waging war," with "the steering wheel turned only to the right."

Article 9 of Japan's Constitution stipulates that the country "forever renounces war as a sovereign right of the nation" and the threat or use of force as a means of settling international disputes. It also states that Japan will not maintain land, sea or air forces or other war potential, nor recognize the right of belligerency of the state. The article is widely regarded as the cornerstone of Japan's postwar pacifist policy.

items.title: Metis TechBio plans A-share listing
text: Metis TechBio Co Ltd, a Beijing-based biotechnology company specializing in drug delivery, has begun preparations for a potential A-share listing on the Chinese mainland, about six months after making its Hong Kong debut.

In a filing to the Hong Kong Stock Exchange on Wednesday, the company said its board had approved preparatory work for issuing renminbi-denominated ordinary shares and appointed an institution to provide pre-listing guidance.

If completed, the proposed listing would allow Metis to tap both the mainland and Hong Kong capital markets, broadening its fundraising channels and investor base. The company gave no fundraising target, exchange or timetable, and said the plan remains subject to shareholder and regulatory approvals.

Founded in 2020, Metis uses artificial intelligence to develop drug delivery technologies, including lipid nanoparticles designed to transport medicines to specific tissues and cells. Its NanoForge platform combines computational modeling with laboratory testing to develop delivery systems.

The company made its Hong Kong trading debut on May 13, offering about 201.2 million shares at HK$10.50 each and raising approximately HK$2.11 billion ($271 million) in gross proceeds before any over-allotment.

Metis reported revenue of 154.3 million yuan ($21.7 million) in the first half of 2026, up from 1.1 million yuan a year earlier, mainly driven by research collaborations and licensing activities. Its net loss attributable to shareholders stood at 153.2 million yuan.
The company reported financial resources totaling 3.03 billion yuan at the end of June, including cash, deposits and financial assets.
In October, Metis announced a collaboration with US pharmaceutical company Eli Lilly to develop tissue-specific lipid nanoparticle delivery technology.

Under the agreement, Metis is set to receive an upfront payment in the low double-digit millions of dollars and could earn up to approximately $1.1 billion in additional payments tied to development and commercial milestones.

items.title: China’s Cargo Drones Take Off With Two Successful Trials
items.link: https://www.sixthtone.com/news/1019298/China’s Cargo Drones Take Off With Two Successful Trials
text: China has successfully tested two large unmanned cargo aircraft: one with a 5-ton payload capacity and the other capable of flying 3,000 kilometers, laying the groundwork for future commercial and emergency transportation systems.

On Tuesday, the country announced that the Changying-8, a domestically developed unmanned cargo aircraft, had completed a test delivery. Three days prior, another domestically developed unmanned cargo aircraft, the W5000, also completed its maiden flight.

The milestones come as China’s drone market is expected to exceed 140 billion yuan ($19.6 billion) by the end of 2026, with the industrial drone segment alone projected to reach 84 billion yuan, up 12.5% from last year.

China began testing large cargo drones as early as 2017 and incorporated the concept of the “low-altitude economy” into government policy in 2021. The Civil Aviation Administration of China has also laid out a roadmap to establish an air transportation system for unmanned aircraft by 2035.
During its delivery test, the Changying-8, developed by China North Industries Group Corporation, released a cargo pallet at an altitude of 300 meters before returning to its base.

The aircraft, whose maiden flight took place in Zhengzhou, capital of the central Henan province, on March 31, has a maximum range of over 3,000 kilometers, measures 17 meters in length, has a 25-meter wingspan, and an 18-cubic-meter cargo compartment volume, domestic media reported.

In the event of extreme disasters such as earthquakes, floods, and mudslides destroying roads and bridges, the aircraft can be used to transport up to 3.5 metric tons of goods, equal to over 700 disaster-relief tents, the head of the Changying-8’s development team told state news agency Xinhua.
According to its engineers, future applications could include transportation of regional cargo, emergency supplies, and cold-chain deliveries, domestic media reported.
On Saturday, the W5000, an unmanned cargo aircraft developed by Chinese aviation company Air White Whale, also completed its maiden flight in northern China’s Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region.

The aircraft flew for about 30 minutes at an altitude of 1,000 meters, completing a series of test maneuvers before landing. The test focused on the aircraft’s flight stability and the coordinated operation of its propulsion, flight control, electronics, and ground-based monitoring and control systems.

With a maximum payload capacity of 5 metric tons, the W5000 is billed as one of the world’s largest unmanned cargo aircraft by payload capacity. Made of carbon fiber and weighing less than 6 metric tons, the aircraft measures over 22 meters in both length and wingspan and can fly at a cruising speed of 526 kilometers per hour, with a maximum range of 2,600 kilometers, domestic media reported.
Hu Zhendong, founder, chairman, and CEO of Air White Whale, said the W5000 could reduce logistics costs per ton-kilometer by more than 60% compared with comparable crewed cargo aircraft.
The W5000 is expected to begin commercial operation by the end of next year, according to domestic media.
[continua sulla fonte originale]

items.title: Why China’s Latest Blockbuster Game Had a Change of Heart
items.link: https://www.sixthtone.com/news/1019294/Why China’s Latest Blockbuster Game Had a Change of Heart
text: One of the wildest boss fights in China’s latest hack-and-slash blockbuster game begins with a calligraphy brush. Soul, the protagonist of Phantom Blade Zero, released late last month, dots the eyes of a lion-dance head, performing a traditional Chinese ritual believed to awaken the eponymous beast.

Cue the violence. Two performers animate the lion, lunging at Soul with blades spinning on its head and flames pouring from its mouth. The fight then spills onto elevated wooden poles, where Soul and the lion-dance master leap from perch to perch, trading blows to pounding Chinese drums and screaming electric guitar.
In the game its creator originally envisioned, Soul had just 66 lives to survive this fight and every other. Use them up, and hours of progress across the campaign would be gone for good.

The restriction was meant to mirror the game’s story: Soul has just 66 days to find a replacement for his damaged heart. But Beijing-based developer S-Game eventually abandoned the compulsory death limit, introducing three difficulty settings and making the original challenge optional.

S-Game founder Liang Qiwei called the compromise “one of the countless difficult decisions we made in developing Phantom Blade Zero.” His studio spent four years and a reported 300 million to 400 million yuan ($45 million to $60 million) creating a game it hoped would introduce wuxia — Chinese martial arts fantasy — to audiences around the world.

To bring its combat to life, S-Game recruited Hong Kong action star Donnie Yen, enlisted martial arts experts, and brought traditional performers into motion-capture studios. The finished game features more than 50 bosses and 55 weapons, each offering different ways to fight.

The scale of the undertaking drew inevitable comparisons with Black Myth: Wukong, China’s breakout global gaming hit of 2024. Chinese gamers even dubbed Phantom Blade Zero “the village’s second college student,” hoping the conditions for success would align twice.

So far, it has. Video game rating site IGN gave Phantom Blade Zero a 9 out of 10, praising its “memorable boss fights, compelling combat, and limitless swagger.” Its PC version scored 88 on review aggregator Metacritic, surpassing the 81 Black Myth: Wukong received.

Released on Oct. 29, with a standard edition priced at 268 yuan ($40) and a deluxe edition at 328 yuan, the game sold more than 4 million copies in its first 72 hours, topping Steam’s bestseller chart and generating an estimated 1 billion yuan in gross sales.

Unlike Wukong, which drew on the beloved Chinese classic “Journey to the West,” Phantom Blade Zero had to win over players with a far less familiar fictional universe, one Liang had spent two decades developing.

In 2006, while studying architecture at Beijing’s Tsinghua University, Liang began developing Rain Blood, an independent role-playing game inspired by Taiwanese wuxia novelist Gu Long. Built using software intended for amateur game developers, it introduced Soul, an assassin serving the Order, a secretive organization of martial artists.

items.title: China Proposes Tougher Rules to Curb Skills Certification Fraud
items.link: https://www.sixthtone.com/news/1019293/China Proposes Tougher Rules to Curb Skills Certification Fraud
text: China has proposed its first regulation on vocational skills certifications, cracking down on fraudulent credentials and tightening oversight of certification bodies.
The Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security released the draft regulation on Nov. 12, with public feedback open until Dec. 12. No date has been set for when the rules will take effect.

China now has more than 220 million skilled workers — including electricians, AI trainers, and elderly-care workers — accounting for about 30% of its workforce, according to the ministry. Vocational skills certificates can bring benefits such as cash subsidies, children’s school enrollment, and fast-tracked residency applications.
Fraudulent vocational skills certificates have proliferated online in recent years, prompting a nationwide crackdown on bogus credentials in 2022.

The proposed regulation would tighten oversight of certification bodies, barring them from making misleading claims or leaking exam questions. In addition, certificates can be issued only to candidates who pass the required assessments, rather than those who simply pay to obtain them.

The draft also outlines that organizations responsible for vocational qualification assessments would be barred from offering related training. Institutions that issue certificates without first registering with the government, as well as those that forge, alter, or trade certificates, may face suspension, confiscation of illegal earnings, and fines of 10,000 to 100,000 yuan ($1,500 to $15,000).

The rules also outline penalties for examiners who engage in misconduct, candidates who cheat, and officials who fail to perform their duties properly. Employers will be encouraged to use workers’ certified skill levels as a key factor in determining pay.

Previously, workers obtained vocational qualifications through government-organized exams. Starting in 2020, however, China phased out most government-issued vocational qualifications, shifting responsibility to registered and supervised third-party organizations. By the end of 2025, 32,000 such organizations were in operation nationwide.

Cheng Xiezhong, a law professor at the China University of Political Science and Law, told domestic media that the shift had “helped expand the pool of skilled workers” but had also led to uneven standards among certification bodies and a widespread increase in bogus certificates.

An investigation by domestic media this June found vocational certificates openly advertised on multiple Chinese e-commerce platforms. In one case, a reporter paid just 300 yuan for a mechanical equipment installer certificate showing passing scores on tests they had never taken.

Previous reports also found that some training providers issued course completion certificates rather than recognized vocational credentials. Others lured young jobseekers into “training loan” scams, persuading them to borrow thousands of yuan for courses.

items.title: Bot, Interrupted: DeepSeek Users Report New Limits on Free Chats
items.link: https://www.sixthtone.com/news/1019284/Bot, Interrupted: DeepSeek Users Report New Limits on Free Chats
text: Chinese AI model DeepSeek has reportedly begun limiting use of its free chatbot by reducing the number of characters users can input and discontinuing inactive conversations after seven days.

DeepSeek users began reporting seeing an error message — “Due to server overload, the use limit has been reached” — on Monday when they tried to continue chats inactive for a week or when they tried to input larger volumes of text, according to posts on microblogging platform Weibo.

According to domestic media, users of the large language model (LLM) can now only enter around 40,000 characters at a time (a page of Chinese text typically ranges from 500 to 800 characters). Previously, the chatbot had no publicly stated text limit. Once users reach their daily limit, DeepSeek displays an error message.
It is reportedly the first time DeepSeek, headquartered in China’s eastern city of Hangzhou, has restricted free-user access since its launch in January 2025.

According to its official status page, DeepSeek has experienced 57 outages or performance degradations this year, without providing additional explanation. Domestic media reported that disruptions in the first half of the year mainly involved slower responses, delays in data generation, and occasional request failures. After October, prolonged global outages began to occur more frequently.

Usage caps apply only to individual users, but because DeepSeek has no related paid plan, those who hit their capacity cannot pay for more. App developers, who pay to use DeepSeek through an application programming interface, or API, a connection that shares data between their software and the AI model, are subject to separate limits and per-use billing.

As of Wednesday, DeepSeek had not announced a reason for the new rules or whether it might lift them. Developers who spotted references to a “Coding Plan” in the website’s code have speculated that the company may soon implement a paid subscription plan for individual users.

Online, users debated the new limits, with many expressing outrage and complaining that the company had not rolled out a paid plan option for individual users before the usage limit. “I feel like I’m a widow who just lost her husband,” wrote one user on lifestyle platform Xiaohongshu, also known as RedNote.

Others sympathized with DeepSeek, arguing that data is costly or hypothesizing that the company was clamping down on users developing companion relationships with its AI, alluding to China’s ban on AI products designed to mimic human personalities that took effect on July 15.

Data from OpenRouter, a U.S.-based platform that provides access to numerous AI models through one interface, showed DeepSeek’s latest model processing 59.2 trillion tokens the week of Nov. 9 to 15, topping OpenRouter’s weekly token usage chart.

Long chats are more costly for LLM developers because models must parse more information with each reply. Industry watchers told domestic media that the higher costs mean DeepSeek may now have to choose between training new models, serving paying API customers, and providing free chats.
[continua sulla fonte originale]

items.title: Lu Xun’s Overlooked Translations That Shaped Modern Chinese Literature
items.link: https://www.sixthtone.com/news/1019257/Lu Xun’s Overlooked Translations That Shaped Modern Chinese Literature
text: In 1903, 22-year-old Lu Xun, then a student in Japan, wandered into a bookstore in Jimbocho, Tokyo’s famed book district, where his attention was caught by a science fiction novel titled “A Journey to the Moon in Ninety-Seven Hours and Twenty Minutes.” Translated into Japanese by Inoue Tsutomu and believed to have been written by an American author, the novel appealed to Lu Xun’s own ambition to popularize scientific knowledge in China, where modern science education was still in its infancy. Enthusiastic about the genre’s potential, he quickly set about translating it into Chinese.

His version, “Yuejie Lüxing” (“A Journey to the Moon”), published the same year and among the earliest Chinese translations of science fiction, marked the beginning of his prolific career as a translator, long before he became celebrated as the “founding father of modern Chinese literature” for his novels and essays.

Today, we know that Inoue had misidentified the original author. The novel was, in fact, Jules Verne’s “De la Terre à la Lune: trajet direct en 97 heures 20 minutes,” published in 1865 and widely translated into English in the 1870s. Misled by its setting — in post-Civil War America, where members of the Baltimore Gun Club plan to fire a projectile at the moon — Inoue assumed the author was American. Lu Xun, following this assumption, opened his translation with original passages describing America in extravagant detail to provide context for his Chinese readers.

The curious story of this translation and mistranslation of Verne’s novel illuminates how literary forms and ideas traveled across borders at the turn of the 20th century, particularly in East Asia following the First Sino-Japanese War (1894–1895), when waves of Chinese students — including Lu Xun — went to study in Japan.

It was in Tokyo, amid the intellectual riches of Jimbocho, where he spent much of his leisure time, that Lu Xun was drawn to translation. Japan’s Meiji Restoration, which restored imperial rule in 1868, had already spurred a flood of translations from European languages into Japanese. Eager to take advantage of this wealth of material, Lu Xun, by then proficient in Japanese, with a working knowledge of German and some Russian, immersed himself in these texts. On one hand, he translated texts from cultures he perceived as more scientifically and technologically advanced, with the aim of promoting science education among his own people; on the other hand, he gradually developed an interest in writers from marginalized communities and nations, believing their experiences would resonate with China, which had endured decades of foreign invasion and exploitation. Later, recounting his decision to translate the exiled Russian writer and activist Vasily Eroshenko, he made clear that he saw translation not simply as an aesthetic pursuit, but as a means of giving voice to the oppressed.
[continua sulla fonte originale]

items.title: Lesson in Endurance: China’s Schools Start Later to Ease Burden on Students
items.link: https://www.sixthtone.com/news/1019288/Lesson in Endurance: China’s Schools Start Later to Ease Burden on Students
text: Parents across China have for years raised concerns about how long children spend in school each day, with some high school students logging at least 15 hours in class.
In recent weeks, education authorities nationwide have been pushing back start times for all grades to ease the burden.

Schools in Nanjing, capital of the eastern Jiangsu province, reportedly began introducing changes in November. A parent told the Yangtze Evening Post that their child, a high school freshman, now starts studying at 7:15 a.m. and finishes after-school study sessions at 9:20 p.m., a 45-minute reduction from the previous schedule of 6:40 a.m. to 9:30 p.m.

Jiangyin, a city about two hours east by road, also announced across-the-board adjustments on Nov. 5. Classes now start at 8 a.m. at primary schools, 7:40 a.m. at middle schools, and 7:20 a.m. at high schools.

During an edition of the show “Zhengfeng Hotline” broadcast live on Jiangsu TV on Oct. 27, Jiang Yong, director of the provincial education department, said, “The issue of excessively long school hours is severe. As the education authority, we feel a profound sense of remorse.”

According to the 2022 China Family Panel Studies (CFPS), a nationally representative longitudinal survey of families, individuals, and communities conducted by researchers at Peking University, 46% of full-time high school students study for more than 12 hours on a typical weekday, while for nearly 25% it’s over 14 hours. Including weekdays and rest days, high school students average 68.6 hours of study time per week.

For a 2026 article published in Youth Studies, researchers from Renmin University of China and Peking University analyzed survey data relating to students aged 6 to 17. They found that high school students spend on average 10 hours and 54 minutes engaged in education-related activities on weekdays and six hours and 29 minutes on weekends. That adds up to about 67.5 hours.
These activities cover in-class instruction, after-class study, off-campus tutoring, and commuting to and from school.
However, for some, 67.5 hours is merely a baseline. The study reveals a direct correlation between a parent’s education level and how long their child spends studying.

For those with only a middle school education or lower, their children study an average of eight hours and two minutes a day. If the parent holds a high school diploma or a university degree, that time rises by 15 or 29 minutes, respectively.
Study time also varies by location and school quality.

The CFPS shows that high school students in China’s four municipalities — Beijing, Shanghai, Tianjin, and Chongqing — as well as provincial capitals study 73.5 hours a week, nearly five hours more than the national average. Meanwhile, for students at key schools, which receive preferential funding and attract high-quality teachers, the figure rises to 75.1 hours.
Both comparisons suggest students in urban high schools and top-tier institutions endure a heavier academic burden.
[continua sulla fonte originale]

items.title: China’s Basic Insurance to Cover CAR T-Cell Cancer Therapy
items.link: https://www.sixthtone.com/news/1019275/China’s Basic Insurance to Cover CAR T-Cell Cancer Therapy
text: China will include a CAR T-cell therapy in its national health insurance scheme for the first time, making a blood cancer treatment that once cost over 1 million yuan ($150,000) per dose more accessible.

The National Healthcare Security Administration announced on Nov. 14 that relmacabtagene autoleucel, or relma-cel, made by Shanghai-based biotech firm JW Therapeutics and sold under the brand name Carteyva, will be covered by insurance starting Jan. 1. The therapy has three approved uses for different types of lymphoma and costs 1.29 million yuan per dose.

CAR T-cell therapy is primarily used to treat types of lymphoma and involves extracting and genetically modifying a patient’s own immune cells to target cancer cells, before infusing them back into the body. China approved its first CAR T-cell therapy product in 2021.

Most of China’s population is covered by the country’s national insurance scheme: 1.33 billion were enrolled in basic medical insurance by the end of 2025. Only drugs listed in the national insurance catalog can be partially reimbursed through the medical insurance fund. For drugs not listed, patients must usually bear 100% of the cost.

For years, CAR T-cell drugs were excluded from the national insurance list because an unwritten industry rule held that drugs priced above 300,000 yuan rarely secured coverage, limiting patient access, according to Shanghai-based media outlet The Paper.

The rate of CAR T-cell drug use as a second-line treatment for large B-cell lymphoma in China is about one-sixth of that in the United States, while use as a third-line treatment is about one-10th of the rate in the U.S. and Europe.

Carteyva was one of five CAR T-cell therapies included last year in China’s first commercial insurance list for high-cost innovative drugs. This year, those drugs became eligible for national coverage. Two CAR T-cell drug manufacturers, including JW Therapeutics, entered insurance coverage negotiations on Sept. 6.
“Two or three years ago, we wouldn’t have dared to imagine this,” Tian Feng, JW Therapeutics chairman and CEO, told The Paper.
China records about 101,500 new lymphoma cases each year. Carteyva is available at more than 200 certified hospitals nationwide.

The updated national reimbursement list adds 107 drugs covering oncology, chronic diseases, mental illnesses, rare diseases, and pediatric medications. A separate commercial insurance list, which covers drugs outside the basic scheme, includes 12 new treatments.

“This is a historic moment for lymphoma patients in China,” Tian said, adding that when he and the company received the news, “everyone really felt that the treatment of lymphoma patients in China had entered a new, very exciting era.”

items.title: China unveils 34 new flagship smart factories, highlighting AI-driven transformation
text: China on Thursday unveiled 34 flagship smart factories across 20 provincial-level regions, expanding the initiative into more consumer-facing industries as the country steps up efforts to integrate artificial intelligence (AI) technology into manufacturing, boost productivity and accelerate the digital transformation of its industrial sector.

The Ministry of Industry and Information Technology (MIIT) and five other departments released the 2026 flagship smart factory cultivation list, which includes major manufacturers such as Xiaomi Auto. Pharmaceutical and apparel manufacturers were included for the first time, highlighting the initiative's widening industry coverage.

As the second batch of flagship smart factories, they have reported an average 34.4 percent increase in labor productivity and a 19.3 percent rise in production efficiency, while helping nearly 4,000 enterprises carry out digital and intelligent transformation in coordination.

Notably, industry coverage has further expanded compared with the previous batch. Beyond equipment manufacturing, steel, electronic information and other fields, pharmaceutical and apparel enterprises in the consumer goods sector were included for the first time, according to the list released by the MIIT.

The list includes smart factory projects from leading Chinese manufacturers across the vehicle, power equipment and shipbuilding sectors, including Xiaomi Auto, FAW-Volkswagen, Harbin Electric Machinery and Hudong-Zhonghua Shipbuilding.

The announcement by the six departments calls for supporting flagship smart factories in building high-quality industrial datasets, developing industrial AI agents, exploring advanced manufacturing models and establishing smart supply chains. The requirements highlight a broader shift in smart factory development, from equipment automation toward deeper integration of AI, industrial data and supply chain coordination.
The MIIT announced 15 candidate factories on November 24, 2025, so the latest batch brings the total number to 49.

Li Changan, a professor at the School of Public Administration at the University of International Business and Economics, told the Global Times on Thursday that the integration of AI with manufacturing is a major technological force driving the development of modern manufacturing.

The inclusion of pharmaceutical and apparel manufacturers in the latest list shows that AI technologies are expanding beyond a limited number of industries and becoming increasingly integrated into traditional manufacturing sectors, according to Li.

The expert further noted that the list not only reflects the progress of AI applications in manufacturing, but also serves as a demonstration and a model for the wider industry, encouraging more traditional manufacturers to accelerate technological upgrades and transformation. This trend is expected to further strengthen China's manufacturing capabilities, improve product quality and enhance the global competitiveness of its manufacturing sector.

items.title: China’s vehicle export trains hit 10,000 trip milestone amid surging overseas demand
text: China's dedicated freight trains carrying domestically manufactured vehicles for export have made a cumulative 10,000 trips, a milestone in the country's expanding automobile exports as growing overseas demand and improving international logistics networks support the industry's global expansion.

The milestone was reached on Thursday when a train carrying 203 Chinese-made new-energy vehicles (NEVs) departed from Zhengzhou International Land Port in Central China's Henan Province, CCTV News reported. The vehicles will travel by rail to Shanghai before being loaded onto a roll-on/roll-off vessel bound for Australia, a journey of more than 10,000 kilometers.

The accelerating rail services reflect robust overseas demand for Chinese-made vehicles. More than 2.035 million vehicles have been transported for export by rail so far this year, up 79 percent year-on-year, according to CCTV News.

The growth comes amid a broader expansion in China's automobile exports. The country exported 9.271 million vehicles in the first 10 months of 2026, up 65.1 percent year-on-year, according to data from the China Association of Automobile Manufacturers released on November 11.

NEV exports reached 4.612 million units during the period, rising 130 percent year-on-year. October alone saw exports of 1.066 million vehicles, marking the fifth consecutive month that shipments exceeded 1 million units.

China's expanding presence in overseas markets has provided further momentum. Industry data showed that Brazil, Belgium, the UK, Australia and Thailand were among the leading destinations for Chinese NEV exports in the first nine months, reflecting demand across Latin America, Europe and the Asia-Pacific region.
Improvements in cross-border logistics have strengthened the industry's export capacity.

To meet growing demand for vehicle exports, railway operators have expanded regular routes through land ports including Horgos, Manzhouli and Alashankou, while using the China-Laos Railway to reach Southeast Asian markets. Combined with expanding rail-sea intermodal services, these routes are strengthening international logistics links for Chinese automakers, a Chinese expert noted.

The expansion of transport capacity and more efficient rail-sea connections are helping Chinese automakers reach overseas customers, underscoring how manufacturing competitiveness and logistics infrastructure are supporting the industry's growing role in global markets, Zhang Xiang, a visiting professor in the engineering department of Zhengzhou-based Huanghe Science and Technology University, told the Global Times on Thursday.

items.title: Press conference for AIE Expo 2026 held in Macao
text: The press conference for the 2026 Global Artificial Intelligence Manufacturing and Electronics Expo (AIE Expo 2026) was held in China's Macao Special Administrative Region (SAR) on November 13, bringing together technology companies from across the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area (GBA) to showcase their latest innovations.

Organizers also outlined the expo's preparations and plans for international cooperation. Wong Yee Lam, a member of the Commerce and Investment Promotion Institute of the Macao SAR, attended the event.

AIE Expo 2026 will take place from December 3 to 5 in Macao and Zhuhai, a city in south China's Guangdong Province. The event aims to serve as a platform for showcasing the latest achievements in China's intelligent manufacturing.

It is expected to attract more than 1,000 technology companies, feature over 20,000 products, and welcome 50,000 industry professionals from China and abroad. More than 100 new products and technologies are scheduled to make their global debuts.

The Zhuhai venue will focus on four industrial sectors, including manufacturing, mobility, living, and electronics, with an emphasis on supply chains and business matchmaking, while the Macao venue will feature four interactive experience zones and six exhibition zones, offering immersive demonstrations and displays of emerging technologies.

At the press conference, companies from Guangzhou, Zhuhai and other cities in the GBA presented innovations in smart healthcare, smart home technologies, cloud computing, and artificial intelligence (AI).

Chen Haibin, a representative of Guangzhou-based Gamsing Technology Co., Ltd., said that moving innovation from the laboratory to the production line requires bringing together cutting-edge technologies, a well-integrated supply chain and real market demand.

He noted that AIE Expo's approach, which combines frontier technology showcases in Macao with targeted business matchmaking in Zhuhai, could help bridge the gap between technological innovation and industrial application.

Confirmed exhibitors include HONOR, OPPO, TCL, Haier, Gree, Tesla, NIO, GAC International, EHang, Jaten Robotics, and XAG, spanning sectors such as intelligent manufacturing, smart mobility, smart living, next-generation electronics, embodied AI and computing hardware.
Professional buyers from Europe, the United States, the Middle East, Africa, and ASEAN have already registered to attend.
A series of business matchmaking sessions will help exhibitors connect with potential buyers across these key sectors.

Leveraging Macao's role as a platform for commercial and trade cooperation between China and Portuguese-speaking countries, the expo aims to deepen collaboration in technological innovation and industrial development between the two sides.

items.title: China commits to low-carbon electrification and help for others to improve
text: Exclusive: Countries at Cop31 are being urged to commit to deriving 35% of their energy from electricity by 2035

China is pushing for rapid electrification of its economy using low-carbon energy and will help other countries do the same, a senior member of the Chinese delegation at the Cop31 UN climate summit has said.

Wang Yi, a professor of energy and environment policy at the Chinese Academy of Sciences and a senior adviser to China’s government, said: “End-use electrification is a very clear direction. We can follow this direction while making the source of electricity clean. That’s the way to go forward.”
China is the biggest emitter of greenhouse gases by far, producing more than a quarter of the world’s total, so its push for electrification is significant.

At Cop31, countries are being asked to sign up to a target of deriving 35% of final energy consumption from electricity by 2035. Australia, the president of the negotiations, and the host nation Turkey have pushed the target and on Friday night Australia and China signed a joint statement endorsing the “35:35” goal.

But in the second draft text of the probable outcome from Cop31, released on Thursday, the electrification pledge was downgraded to one of a suite of voluntary options countries can take up to reduce their greenhouse gas emissions.

In an interview with the Guardian at the talks, Wang said: “China will do our best to realise clean end-use electrification, and also help other countries to improve. China has significantly reduced the cost of clean technology and products and we would like to share our experience with other countries.”

Experts have said electrification is the next vital step in the shift to a low-carbon economy, as the only way to diminish the close to 80% of fossil fuels still used for primary energy, mostly for transport, heating and industry.

While civil society organisations want any commitment made on electrification to specify that it must be met from clean sources, a pledge that leaves the choice to countries is likely to have more widespread support, as many – including China and India – are resistant to anything they feel smacks of “top down” interference in national plans.

But campaigners argue that allowing individual countries to decide risks leaving the door open to more gas-fired power plants. Some compromise language is also possible that would urge countries to decarbonise their power.

Last year, electricity made up nearly 30% of China’s energy use and it is on track to make that 35% by 2030. Electricity is several times more efficient than fossil fuels, meaning that it takes far less energy to run electric vehicles, heat pumps and industrial processes than their fossil fuel counterparts.

Wang said China was happy with the 2035 target, but that it would be harder to meet if the electricity was required to come entirely from low-carbon sources. “For this target, no problem. But if you think about ensuring clean electrification, that may be a little bit difficult, even for China. For other countries, it’s even more difficult,” he said.

Can Chinese tech companies help the country achieve technological self-reliance while keeping up in the AI arms race? On this episode, we speak with Kyle Chan, a fellow at the Brookings Institution’s John L. Thornton China Center and author of the High Capacity newsletter, about Beijing’s response to the global AI boom and the tensions between Chinese companies’ commercial ambitions and the government’s long-term plans. items.title: How China is using summits to expand its global influence
text: SHENZHEN, China — For a second year in a row, Chinese President Xi Jinping has brought Russian President Vladimir Putin together with another major world leader on mainland Chinese shores.

U.S. President Donald Trump had a trilateral meeting with Xi and Putin on Thursday, after the three met the prior evening during a welcome banquet for the Asia-Pacific Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen. It marked the first time they had met together in person.

In September 2025, Xi, Putin and Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi briefly laughed together for a friendly photo-op alongside an annual meeting of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization in Tianjin, China. The gathering followed easing tensions between Beijing and New Delhi.

China's "ability to engage directly with the world major powers" reflects the country's influence across the Global South and Eurasia, said Jodie Wen, postdoctoral fellow at the Center for International Security and Strategy at Tsinghua University. "China hopes to play a more constructive role in this conflict-[ridden], unstable world."
In the future, "China will hope to provide more platforms" within its borders for countries to discuss issues, she said.

By participating in and hosting different multilateral organizations, China has stayed in the Western orbit while cultivating relations with non-Western countries. The two photo-ops last year and this year reflect only a portion of Xi's large number of meetings with different world leaders.

Xi has hosted more than 40 heads of state so far this year, including at least eight around the APEC meetings in Shenzhen this week. That's on top of receiving over 60 state visits in 2025, according to CNBC analysis of official Chinese readouts.
Domestic Chinese media have highlighted how Xi has met with many foreign leaders around the China-hosted events.

"Beijing sees these multilateral platforms as opportunities to expand its international influence and demonstrate its commitment to multilateralism, while bilateral diplomacy remains equally important," said Yue Su, principal economist for China at EIU.
But she noted that different countries increasingly pursue different geopolitical and economic priorities, making it challenging to reach consensus even through multilateral organizations.

items.title: China’s Top Planner Seeks Faster Construction of State Projects
text: China’s top planning agency urged local authorities to speed up the construction of government investment projects and disbursement of funds in a bid to spur growth in the world’s second-largest economy.

The National Development and Reform Commission also called for stronger monitoring and coordination among local governments to accelerate construction and funding to generate more on-the-ground activity as quickly as possible, it said in a statement posted on its WeChat account on Saturday. Local authorities were told to step up preparatory work and strengthen strategic planning to improve the quality of projects in the pipeline.
